processing: Little is documented about the protected tea's method. As with other Guizhou greens, expect heat-fixing, shaping and drying; the same plant is also made into black tea.
harvest_season: Not specifically recorded. A spring picking is usual for Guizhou greens.
appearance_dry: Not well described in print; expect a green, twisted or curled leaf as with other regional greens.
appearance_liquor: Not specifically described; a clear yellow-green is typical of Guizhou greens.
taste_profile: Tasting notes for the green tea are scarce. Black tea from the same plant has been tested as sweet, mellow and strong, sweeter and softer than Yunnan large-leaf black tea.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Guizhou green, not a recorded local method. Adjust by taste, especially with old-tree material.

vintage_note: Little is recorded about how it is sold. A green sold under this name should carry the current spring harvest and be drunk within the year; Pu'an black tea from the same plant is a separate product.
description:
Pu'an Siqiu Tea comes from Pu'an county in southwest Guizhou and takes its name from the Siqiu tea plant, Camellia tetracocca. The plant, not the processing, is what makes it distinct, and local descriptions connect the tea with very old trees.

The protected tea's method is little documented. Much of the recent attention is on the plant itself, with Guizhou University and the county working together on conserving and using this old-tree material.

The best tasting evidence is for black tea rather than green: a 2025 study found Siqiu black tea sweet and mellow, with less caffeine and more soluble sugar than Yunnan large-leaf black tea. That may not carry over to a green. For the green, start with moderately hot water and taste as you go.

Check the label carefully. The Pu'an tea name also covers black tea, so a packet may be green or black, and claims about tree age deserve some scepticism unless the seller can back them up.
history:
Local descriptions speak of thousand-year-old tea trees as the source of this tea, though that is a promotional claim as much as a measured one. On firmer ground, geographical indication protection was approved on 4 July 2016, covering 12 towns and subdistricts of Pu'an county.

In April 2026 Pu'an hosted the first national conference on old-tree tea, where the county signed agreements with Guizhou University on conserving Siqiu tea germplasm and bringing new varieties into production.
